title: Whole Biaxial Chevron Plate and Zigzag Edge Canopy
description: One wholly newly authored complete static biaxial folded-plate canopy. Forty-eight planar parallelogram top facets join edge to edge as one continuous finite-thickness roof material boundary, with the full matching folded underside and complete narrow terminal thickness faces. Alternating shear across six rows bends the crease paths into a true two-axis chevron pattern rather than independent straight corrugations. Two whole continuous constant-level edge girders follow the zigzag plan edges from end to end; four full-height corner piers on separate broad soles and four complete longitudinal knee braces support the displayed arrangement. Unlike the earlier three separate asymmetric sawtooth roof plates over eight columns, this is a single closed plate folded in two directions, with no vertical clerestory strips, opaque window panes, triangular monitor trusses or factory floor. Unlike the two-layer pyramid space grid, its roof is a continuous face-bearing solid rather than independent bars and open lattice cells. All numeric roof, matching underside, edge beams, piers and braces authored together; no old roof panel, pavilion frame or origami mesh imported or extracted. Four opaque constant PBR roles, metres Z up, full horizontal bounds centred over four ground soles, one architectural module zero scenes. The chevron pattern is a fixed geometric artwork, not a proven rigid-folding mechanism or fabrication pattern. No unfolding, hinge motion, flat-foldability, drainage, weather sealing, plate stiffness, buckling, span, structural load, wind rating, fabrication, installation, building-code or safety capability made or verified. No walls, occupants, rigging, animation or interaction.
